clue.text: Kipling poem about the French being useless

indicators.note: about means the poem's title goes around the French article here

parts.note: Boots is a Kipling poem about marching soldiers
les is French for the

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a Kipling poem about France as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootless is an old word for unavailing or pointless, from boot meaning profit.

clue.text: Disregard amnesty

explanation.surface: Ignoring offences is what a general pardon amounts to.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is a state of being forgotten or ignored, and historically an Act of Oblivion granted a pardon for past offences.

clue.text: Tread one way round torn lino to get jumper

parts.note: to tramp is to tread heavily

indicators.note: torn says the letters of lino and one are ripped up and reassembled

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone walks round a ripped floor covering to fetch a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' scrambles I and LINO into OLINI, and 'round' puts ST around that, after TRAMP. 'jumper' looks like a sweater but is someone who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampolinist bounces on a trampoline, so is a jumper.

clue.text: Hand has to use the middle of the sleeve

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

indicators.note: the middle of says only the central letters of the word sleeve are taken

explanation.surface: A worker has to use the centre of a shirt sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is a worker, as in farmhand, not the thing at the end of a sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a hired worker, a staff member on the payroll.

clue.text: Florence's hospital in a rustic setting

indicators.note: setting means the letters of a rustic are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Florence Nightingale's hospital stood in countryside surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence Nightingale nursed soldiers of the Crimean War at the barracks hospital at Scutari, near Constantinople.
explanation.definitionFit: Scutari was the site of the military hospital where Florence Nightingale worked.

clue.text: In a hollow, a lily out of scripture

indicators.note: out of says the lily stands outside, around the scripture abbreviation

parts.note: an arum is a kind of lily
NT is the New Testament, scripture

explanation.surface: A lily grows in a dip, sprung from holy writ.
explanation.definitionFit: An antrum is an anatomical cavity, such as a sinus.

clue.text: Peak in Thessaly, exceptionally big when climbing

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, exceptionally big

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word for when is read upwards

parts.note: as can mean when

explanation.surface: A Greek mountain looks enormous to someone going up it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is a mountain in Thessaly, famed in myth for being piled on Pelion.

clue.text: Conditions difficult to endure in an ironclad?

explanation.surface: Life aboard an armoured warship was tough to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as hard ship, a fair description of an armoured vessel; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship means suffering or privation; an ironclad is a warship plated with iron, a ship that is hard.

clue.text: She has a title to property returned after a swindle

indicators.note: after says the returned property comes behind the swindle

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: returned means the word for property is read backwards

parts.note: an asset is a piece of property

explanation.surface: A titled woman gets her estate back after being defrauded.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a woman with a noble rank.

clue.text: Group of people applauded the defence

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gathering clapped the barrister's case for the accused.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is what a defendant puts forward in answer to a charge, the defence's case.

clue.text: Top brass ensemble?

parts.note: top brass suggests senior officers, and a brass ensemble is a group of players, so a group of musicians belonging to the forces

explanation.definitionFit: A regimental band plays brass instruments and belongs to the armed forces, whose leaders are called top brass.

clue.text: Turn left — there's clearly trouble back along the line

definitions.text: there's clearly trouble back along the line

parts.note: a bend is a turn
sinister is Latin and heraldic for left

explanation.surface: A driver turning left senses an accident behind on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry this diagonal band is popularly taken as the mark of illegitimacy, so trouble back along the family line.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic band running from upper right to lower left traditionally signalled a bastard descent in one's ancestry.

clue.text: Simple fellow, head of the Yard, buying promotion

parts.note: Simple Simon is the nursery-rhyme simpleton

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word Yard is taken

explanation.surface: A naive man and a Scotland Yard chief are caught buying advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the buying or selling of church offices, purchasing preferment.

clue.text: Classical school language

parts.note: Roman describes classical antiquity

explanation.surface: A school of classics teaches a tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Romansch is a Romance tongue spoken in parts of Switzerland.

clue.text: Agent in disguise sounds the tocsin perhaps

indicators.note: disguise means the letters of agent and in are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A spy in disguise rings the alarm bell.
explanation.walkthrough: A tocsin is an alarm bell; an antigen is what sets off the body's immune alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a substance that triggers an immune response, figuratively raising the alarm.

clue.text: Resident Magistrate in "As You Like It" has a way with officers' names

indicators.note: in says the magistrate abbreviation goes inside the play's initials

parts.note: AYLI are the initials of the Shakespeare comedy
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A magistrate appearing in a Shakespeare comedy knows how to handle officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Army List is the official published roll of commissioned officers.

clue.text: Neat petticoat in primrose

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a cow
a slip is a petticoat

explanation.surface: A tidy underskirt in pale yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy but is the archaic word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild plant of the primula family, a kind of primrose.

clue.text: Spoke freely and took the lid off riding

parts.note: to take a lid off is to open something
up means on horseback, riding, as in a jockey being up

explanation.surface: Someone talked candidly and uncovered things while on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to talk without reserve.

clue.text: Just begun a nice hot rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters of a nice hot are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has just started on a pleasant hot rum drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the old adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means only just started, not yet fully formed.

clue.text: Seek nut to make into carved ornament

indicators.note: make into says the letters of seek nut are turned into something new

explanation.surface: Find a nut to whittle into a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A netsuke is a small carved Japanese toggle, often of ivory or wood.

clue.text: Transmit unit sign for a return by sea

indicators.note: for a return means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to transmit
I is one, a unit
the Ram is the zodiac sign Aries

explanation.surface: Instructions to transmit a call sign so a ship can head home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a return' turns the whole run EMIT, I, RAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means relating to the sea or seafaring.

clue.text: Diamond case where you keep things

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a box is a case

explanation.surface: A jewel casket for storing valuables.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a cold cabinet for storing food.

clue.text: Girl wanted for English by university town in France

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: An advertisement seeks a young woman to teach English near a French university town.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a female first name.

clue.text: Having no syllabus, head shows lack of enthusiasm

parts.note: a syllabus is a list, so having none is being without a list
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A head teacher without a curriculum seems apathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Listlessness is languor, an absence of energy or interest.

clue.text: Examine and test the meter, say

explanation.surface: Inspect and check the gas reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meter' looks like a gauge, but it is the American spelling of verse metre.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to inspect closely, and also to analyse the metrical pattern of verse.

clue.text: Electric car the auction room rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the word for the auction room is turned back

parts.note: a mart is a salesroom or auction room

explanation.surface: An auction house turned down an electric vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a streetcar running on rails, usually powered by overhead wires.

clue.text: False stone in emblem

parts.note: sham means false or fake
a rock is a stone

explanation.surface: A fake gem set in a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the national badge of Ireland.

clue.text: Religious book returned as not wanted is sold abroad

parts.note: Ex is the abbreviation for Exodus, a book of the Bible

indicators.note: returned means the phrase for not wanted is read backwards

parts.note: de trop is French, used in English, for unwanted or superfluous

explanation.surface: A holy book sent back as unwanted is shipped overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods exported are sent to another country for sale.
